messages.subject: Poppr version 2.1 has been released
messages.body_plain:
Poppr version 2.1 has officially been released onto CRAN. Windows and OSX versions should be up in the next few days.

Here's a summary of what's new:

New functions rrmlg, rraf, pgen, psex (Thanks to Stacy A. Krueger-Hadfield and Erik Sotka for providing example code)
New features: greater flexibility in input formats for aboot and msn functions
Speedups: samp.ia, win.ia, genotype_curve (Thanks to Jonah Brooks for help with C code)

You can view all of the changes here: https://github.com/grunwaldlab/poppr/releases/tag/v.2.1.0

Best,
Zhian

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm trying to run bruvo.boot but I got a warning: "some branch lenghts of the tree are negative. Normalizing branches according to Kuhner and Felsenstein. How can I normalized my data?

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] normalizing branches
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

To answer your question, there is nothing you can do to normalize your data, it is a symptom of the tree that's derived, and the normalization is being performed for you.

Details:

Occasionally, calculating a neighbor-joining tree from genetic distances of clonal organisms results in negative branch lengths. Most often these are reflective of clonal pairs and the negative length is extremely close to zero. Since bootstrapping cannot be done with negative branch lengths, these are corrected by borrowing the length from the sibling branch as described in Kuhner and Felsenstein (1994) (http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/8015439) in the section "Correction of Negative Branch Lengths". For the curious, here is how it's implemented currently: https://github.com/grunwaldlab/poppr/blob/05f604f61b414fa432671fd6f9f964ddffdbd9a5/R/internal.r#L1057-L1115

Hope that helps,
Zhian

messages.subject: significant test in Amova and P value
messages.subject_clean: significant test in Amova and P value
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have some issues interpreting my data. I'm running AMOVA, and using the significant test (with 1000 permutation) to determine if my populations are different or not.
>From the AMOVA output, almost 94% of the variation comes from within samples, 6% from between populations.The Phi value, is really low 0.05 within samples and 0.06 between populations. I'll assume with these small Phi values that there is a low level of differentiation in my populations. When I ran the significant test, the p-value for variation within samples is 0.230, supporting the idea that there is no significant population differentiation at this stratification, however, the p value between population is 0.007.
Could be possible to say that we observed significant differentiation between my populations with a p-value of 0.007 and a PHI value of 0.06

messages.subject: Re: significant test in Amova and P value
messages.subject_clean: significant test in Amova and P value
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

This question is general enough that it is outside the scope of this forum (which is mainly for procedural information on poppr and/or bugs). This question is about the output of AMOVA, which is controlled by ade4 or pegas (poppr.amova is a wrapper for both). I would encourage you to post this to the R-SIG-Genetics list: https://stat.ethz.ch/mailman/listinfo/r-sig-genetics

Regarding your question: One thing to consider is asking whether or not within individual variance is important to consider for your inquiry.

Best,
Zhian

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] error message when loading poppr
messages.body_plain:
Hi

This is an issue that appeared with the new version of phangorn (which poppr requires). Basically, the solution is to run the following code to install Biostrings:

source("http://bioconductor.org/biocLite.R")
biocLite("Biostrings")

Zhian

Sent from my iPhone
